title: Week 2 of Agentic Trading, 2 weeks in the green!
author: randbobaccount
selftext:
Week 1: up 6.97% https://www.reddit.com/r/ai\_trading/comments/1vheu4a/week\_1\_of\_agentic\_trading\_mostly\_through/

Week 2: up 3.69%. Mostly the same agents but added a new one from Raijin which tracks truth social and buys the stock if the sentiment is positive.

Going to keep you all updated on how this is going - feel free to join the journey!

comments.author: Sweaty-Regret559
comments.body: How do the rules work for it to take a trade?

replies.author: randbobaccount
replies.body: It depends on the agent, they all have different rule sets across the board. For example the trump tweet agent triggers on a truth social post. If it mentions a company it uses Ai to determine the sentiment and if it should add that to the holding and it’ll automatically buy it for me. The app actually pretty nicely describes each strategy for you before you put money in it

replies.author: Sweaty-Regret559
replies.body: Thats interesting, im very interested in the safety measures of the trade, but maybe thats my issue, simple might be better in this case, as it seems to be working well for you..

replies.author: randbobaccount
replies.body: They have a ton of risk settings actually. Risk caps are there for stop losses/drawdowns. Agents don’t trade anything outside of the universe of stocks it can. And from what I understand it can’t completely flip the portfolio in most cases. Most things are pretty deterministic, only uses ai when necessary which I like. Execution is also separate, so it wouldn’t accidentally trade more than you deployed.

replies.author: Sweaty-Regret559
replies.body: Very cool, I see, im understanding, they provide the tools for AI trading but you set the strategy/settings, ive download a local LLM qwen 3.5 and have been using that + python to create an autonomous trading bot through alpaca, the biggest hurdle i have is the actual strategy, stocks are new to me, as well as python, its a bit a big learning curve for me but im slowly understanding, thanks for thebreplies man I appreciate it

comments.author: Saidherw
comments.body: I want to get started with AI-powered trading. What should I know? Does it cost anything to use Raijin? What is your methodology?

replies.author: randbobaccount
replies.body: Hey, I’d start with Raijin it’s free for the first month and you can get more free months by referring people. It’s a good way to start so you don’t need to set all the infrastructure up yourself. I’ve just been choosing either the top performing agents or agents with strategies I like the most, haven’t really experimented with building out my own yet - I like the selection on Raijin!

replies.author: Saidherw
replies.body: And how much do you recommend starting with? From what I understand, you connect Raijin to Coinbase and Robinhood, correct?

replies.author: randbobaccount
replies.body: Yes connect Raijin with any of your brokerages, it also supports Webull, Moomoo, Kalshi, etc. I’d start with around 30% of the portfolio and scale up over a month, but really up to you on your risk tolerance.
